doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Break in the session; Barnet's gray uniforms
summary: The first session partly inaudible; Barnet dressed Terry and Nottingham in gray, provoking audience protest in Washington.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah, let’s stop for a minute. [Substantial portions of the final 61 minutes of the interview of June 15, 1999, are inaudible.]

[relates a story of Barnet having his two stars, Terry and Jimmy Nottingham, wear gray uniforms, with the rest of the band dressed in blue uniforms.] The people in D.C., they rebelled. They said, “Why do they not have on the same kind of uniforms as the rest of the band? Are they not a part of it?” Charlie had to take those uniforms and dye them, dye them blue.
